guitar.evidence: Brian May's homemade "Red Special" guitar is one of the most iconic and well-documented instruments in rock history.

tone.target: bright Queen rock crunch with clean arpeggio sections
tone.profile: bright Queen rock crunch with clean arpeggio sections
tone.summary: A classic British crunch tone, utilizing a UK-style amp model paired with light overdrive for punchy attack. Modulation is kept minimal to support the 'clean arpeggios' contrast.
corrections: drop chorus as a core effect
use clean arpeggios as a contrast, not a chorus lead

rig.name: Queen - Don't Stop Me Now - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide the necessary 'tight punchy attack' and light overdrive for the crunch sections.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is a general choice; specific British-style tube screamer emulation would be ideal, but this provides the required grit.

blocks.purpose: Bypass or use only for extreme crunch sections (kept off by default).
blocks.gap: No dedicated boost/distortion is needed here as the Green OD handles the primary gain structure.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the British-style, bright rock tone required for Queen's sound.

alternatives.model: UK 45 (for a slightly more aggressive edge)

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British rock cabinet sound and necessary upper-mid punch.
Fine-tune the tone to emphasize bright upper mids and maintain clarity in arpeggios.
Add subtle modulation for depth without sounding like a heavy chorus, supporting the arpeggio contrast.
blocks.gap: The 'Chorus' module is used sparingly to meet the requirement of light modulation only if subtle. Settings are kept low per instructions.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle space and dimension to the arpeggio sections.
